as_told.title: Truman-Forrestal memo and first NSC meeting

plain: The Majestic 12 papers, said to describe a secret group set up to deal with a crashed saucer, include a memo from President Harry Truman to Defense Secretary James Forrestal dated 24 September 1947, and two tellers take its date as a sign that whoever wrote the papers knew real history. A researcher who goes by UAPGerb tells Michels that the papers mention dates when Forrestal and Truman actually met. On a later episode Michels gives the memo's date himself, connects it to the scientist Vannevar Bush and to the first meeting of the National Security Council, the president's top security advisory body, and credits the UFO researcher Stanton Friedman. The memo is attached to a briefing paper for president-elect Dwight Eisenhower dated 18 November 1952. Both turned up on a roll of film a man named Jaime Shandera received anonymously at his Burbank home in 1984, and were made public in 1987. The memo opens "Dear Secretary Forrestal: As per our recent conversation on this matter," and the briefing paper says Truman set up the group "on 24 September, 1947, upon recommendation by Dr. Vannevar Bush and Secretary James Forrestal." So the papers give a date and mention a recent conversation. The claim that this date matches a real meeting of the two men comes from the tellers comparing it with the record of their appointments, and the papers themselves neither confirm nor rule that out. Friedman judged the papers "almost certainly genuine"; a critic named Philip Klass called the Truman memo an obvious fraud, and the FBI's copies are marked "BOGUS."

discussion.text: A typed briefing paper dated 18 November 1952, with a Truman memorandum to Secretary Forrestal of 24 September 1947 as its Attachment A, that came to light on a roll of 35mm film Jaime Shandera received anonymously at his Burbank home in 1984 and that he, William Moore and Stanton Friedman then studied; it was made public in 1987. The National Archives and the Truman and Eisenhower Libraries report their searches for it negative. The FBI's Majestic 12 file holds copies sent to it in 1988 and 1991, each marked "BOGUS" by hand, and records that the Air Force Office of Special Investigations "advised on November 30, 1988, that the document was fabricated" and that "the document is completely bogus". Philip Klass called the Truman memo an obvious fraud; Friedman judged the briefing paper and the memo "almost certainly genuine". Attachment A, the Truman memorandum dated 24 September 1947, is addressed "MEMORANDUM FOR THE SECRETARY OF DEFENSE Dear Secretary Forrestal:" and opens "As per our recent conversati[[on]] on this matt[[er]]" (double brackets mark letters hidden by the stroke on the FBI's one copy); the briefing paper says the group was "established by special classified executive order of President Truman on 24 September, 1947, upon recommendation by Dr. Vannevar Bush and Secretary James Forrestal." The papers give the date and a recent conversation; that the date matches a meeting of the two men is the tellers' comparison with the record of their appointments, which the papers do not hold and neither confirm nor exclude.
